Look at the -Wliteral-conversion warnings dxc prints for the five store() calls in main(),
and compare the "from ... to ..." pair each warning states with the source-comment on the
same line (which names the value the conversion actually produces).

On any line whose literal carries an explicit unary minus (lines 1, 2 and 4 of the shader
body), the printed pair has lost that minus sign on BOTH sides: it reports the same
"from"/"to" magnitudes as if the literal had been positive, so the sign of the reported
result is wrong whenever the true result is negative (line 1) or the true result should
clamp toward the opposite end of the destination range (lines 2 and 4). The two lines
whose literal has no unary minus (the "MaxPositive" cases) report the correct pair.

DXC's own DXIL output for the same file constant-folds each conversion at compile time and
disagrees with the warning on exactly those three lines -- the folded value matches the
source comment, not the warning.
